# META-INSIGHTS — about the optimization PROCESS itself (this run)

Not about the capability — about HOW this run is searching for it: which strategies/edit classes/algorithms are helping vs stalling, and what to try next iteration. Update at the end of the run at minimum; sooner if a plateau or a clear strategy shift is worth recording now. Structure each addition as:

    ## Iteration <id> (or 'run so far')
    - Strategy tried, and whether it moved val (cite LEDGER rows):
    - Plateau/stall signal, if any, and the lever switched to:
    - What to try next iteration:

## Iteration cand_0001 (first iteration of run)
- Strategy tried, and whether it moved val: Diagnosed all 10 failing tasks against gold actions + evaluator source FIRST, then shipped only edits that pass all three tests (REAL/SAFE/VERIFIED). Anchored on two independently-verified deterministic wins (task 40 DB via roster repair, task 11 COMMUNICATE via refund surfacing) plus safe additive enrichments. Val result pending (harness scores after stop).
- Key process finding: The dominant lever here is that the wrapper's forwarded args ARE the graded DB write, so arg normalization/repair (not prose) is what flips DB-basis tasks. COMMUNICATE-basis tasks flip via return-value enrichment that names the exact number to say. Verifying a fix means running the repair on the trajectory's exact failing args and checking it reproduces gold — done offline in /tmp before shipping.
- Plateau/stall signal: none yet (first iteration). Avoided padding the candidate: refused any guard keyed on task-specific ids (wrong-flight/wrong-reservation), because those overfit and fail the held-out gate without helping the class.
- What to try next iteration: read this run's RESULT/LEDGER to confirm which of 40/11/19/37 actually moved; then escalate to a composite atomic-write tool for the narrate-without-execute stall cluster (17/23/25) — the one class a guard can't fix — and gate it on whether the reader selects it.
